facts.statement: The genus Elaphrocnemus was first described by Milne-Edwards in 1891.
Fossils of Elaphrocnemus date from the Middle Eocene to the Late Oligocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Eocene to Late Oligocene

facts.statement: Elaphrocnemus was an extinct bird that lived in Europe during the Eocene and Oligocene periods.
facts.quote: Elaphrocnemus is a genus of extinct bird from the Eocene and Oligocene periods of Europe.

facts.statement: Elaphrocnemus belongs to the order Cariamiformes and is most closely related to modern seriemas.
facts.quote: Part of Cariamiformes, its closest living relatives are seriemas

facts.statement: Unlike its living relatives, Elaphrocnemus was a significantly better flyer.
facts.quote: though it differs significantly from them, being a better flyer

facts.statement: Elaphrocnemus was originally placed in the family Orthocnemidae, which was later absorbed into Idiornithidae.
facts.quote: It was referred to the family Orthocnemidae, since them absorbed into Idiornithidae.

facts.statement: The classification of Elaphrocnemus is debated because recent studies suggest the family Idiornithidae is polyphyletic.
facts.quote: However, relationships within Cariamiformes are unresolved, as several studies render Idiornithidae as polyphyletic

facts.statement: Some researchers consider Elaphrocnemus a synonym of Talantatos, while others treat it as a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Some authorities renders the genus a synonym of Talantatos, though some recent studies recover it as independent from this genus.

facts.statement: Elaphrocnemus had long scapulas similar to those of pelicans, suggesting it was a capable flyer.
facts.quote: Elaphrocnemus appears to have been a good flyer. It possesses long scapulas, convergent in shape to those of pelicans

facts.statement: Despite having a weakly developed furcula like modern seriemas, Elaphrocnemus possessed proportionally large and strong wing bones.
facts.quote: although its furcula was as weakly developed as that of modern seriemas and their flightless relatives it had proportionally large and strong wing bone elements.

facts.statement: Elaphrocnemus had shorter legs than other Cariamiformes, implying it was less adapted for running.
facts.quote: Likewise, its legs were also shorter than those of other Cariamiformes, implying a less cursorial lifestyle.

facts.statement: Elaphrocnemus was one of the most common birds in the Quercy Formation, possibly living in large flocks.
facts.quote: Elaphrocnemus is one of the most common birds in sites like the Quercy Formation, perhaps indicating agglomeration in large flocks.

facts.statement: Elaphrocnemus lived in a subtropical climate that supported a rich rainforest ecosystem with diverse mammals and birds.
facts.quote: The local climate was subtropical in nature, producing a rich rainforest ecosystem that included a large variety of mammal and bird species.
